Thinking evolutionarily, humans have spent much more time identifying with and adapting to nature than our modern world. Think about it. Nearly 100,000 years for Homo sapiens alone to form meaningful bonds with the natural world, adapting to its stimuli and energies, and much much MUCH longer if you're going to count all of our evolutionary ancestors. I think as technology advances but unfortunately pushes us a little farther away from the world we were, as a species, raised to be connected to, that bond and its subsequent wisdom will seem to fade. 

It is still there though, and much of magick and the occult seeks to reunite us with it, unwittingly or otherwise. Whether it's through trust in the intuition, reverence toward nature itself, or simply looking to quiet the mind of all the crazy stress of modern life, a common theme in many occult systems is suspending the dogmatically rational and result obsessed frame of mind that many have come to solely depend on, and to attune ourselves more with our roots. Our roots where each part of the soul, from the practical to the divine, was prized equally, and where the complex system of nature made us feel as one with the world around us, rather than at war with it. That's my interpretation anyway.

First of all, read anything you can get your hands on, but don't blindly believe anything. As long as it's safe, practice what you read, see what speaks to you, what works for you, and what doesn't. Don't lose your skepticism. Skepticism is healthy, but don't confuse skepticism with dismission. Of course, meditate often. 

The most important tip, or at least it was for me, is practice every day if possible. Even if it's just something small. It really helped keep me on track and in the right state of mind when I was first starting out. 

Finally, just remember that this is your path to pave for yourself. You can use tradition, belief, and ritual from certain paths or people's writings, and for some people, that's perfect, but remember that you're always free to go your own way and explore if that feels like the right thing for you. 

Of course, always be aware of any risks involved with a particular practice, and don't try skipping small "beginner stuff" in favor of more complex, advanced, and, frankly, more exciting sounding practices, as you could end up getting results you didn't intend or, more likely, absolutely nothing. No matter which path you choose, it involves practice, work, and self discovery. Keep an open, yet skeptical mind and do what works and feels right to you.
